clue.text: Soldier dead in Italian lake, a raider

indicators.note: in says the soldier and the dead abbreviation sit inside the name of the lake

parts.note: Lake Como is in northern Italy
a man is an ordinary soldier, as in officers and men
d is the standard abbreviation for dead, as on family trees

explanation.surface: A soldier's body found in an Italian lake turns out to have been a raider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the soldier and dead into the lake; the dead soldier in the surface is a red herring, and 'a' is only a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A commando is a soldier trained to carry out swift raids behind enemy lines.

clue.text: Supervise deliveries to bishop's office

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries, so overs stands for deliveries
a see is a bishop's seat or diocese

explanation.surface: Someone is told to keep an eye on the parcels arriving at the bishop's office.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the game played with bat and ball, a bowler's six balls in a row make an OVER, so 'deliveries' are OVERS. A bishop's area of office is his SEE.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversee work is to direct and watch over it, a synonym of supervise.

clue.text: Ugly rumours about editor turning deadly

indicators.note: about says the rearranged letters wrap around the other piece
ugly rumours suggests the letters of rumours turned nasty and out of shape
turning says the abbreviation for editor is read backwards

explanation.surface: Nasty gossip about a newspaper editor takes a deadly turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ugly' rearranges the rumours, 'turning' reverses the editor's abbreviation, and 'about' wraps the first round the second, so the reversed letters sit in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Murderous means capable of killing or intending to kill, hence deadly.

clue.text: Indian leader in favour henceforth, after uprising

indicators.note: after uprising says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An Indian leader is back in favour after a rebellion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points into 'favour henceforth', where URHEN sits; in a down clue 'uprising' turns it to read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Jawaharlal Nehru was the first Prime Minister of independent India.

clue.text: See possible future in a rum old novel such as this?

indicators.note: possible future suggests one of many ways the letters could be arranged

explanation.surface: A fortune teller looks into a strange old novel to see what lies ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possible' rearranges the five words after it; the answer is the title of Charles Dickens's last finished novel, and 'such as this' hints the clue is a puzzle shared between setter and solver.
explanation.definitionFit: Our Mutual Friend is a novel by Charles Dickens, published in 1864-65.

clue.text: European, kind of — could be French

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is the nationality; the second is the shine, since French polish is a well-known type.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Poland is a European, and French polish is a kind of shiny varnish for furniture.

clue.text: Alarm, perhaps, raised over the French in Scottish town

indicators.note: over in a down clue places the first piece above the second
raised in a down clue says the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: a beep is one kind of alarm signal, hence perhaps
les is the French plural word for the

explanation.surface: An alarm goes off above the French in a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns the alarm sound upwards, and in a down clue 'over' puts it above the French article. The answer is a town in the Scottish Borders.
explanation.definitionFit: Peebles is a small town on the River Tweed in the south of Scotland.

clue.text: Truck runs into bird

indicators.note: into says the abbreviation is placed inside the bird's name

parts.note: a lory is a brightly coloured parrot
r is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A truck ploughs into a bird on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes into LORY, a small parrot of Australasia.
explanation.definitionFit: A lorry is the British word for a large goods vehicle, a truck.

clue.text: Newly designed carpets multi-coloured things

indicators.note: newly designed suggests the letters of carpets are given a fresh pattern

explanation.surface: Freshly designed carpets come in many colours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Newly designed' rearranges CARPETS.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectra are the bands of colour into which light is split, as in a rainbow.

clue.text: Man with bequest — he'll take on the taxmen

indicators.note: take on says the second piece is added on after the first

parts.note: he'll supplies the pronoun he
IR stands for the Inland Revenue, the former British tax office

explanation.surface: A man who has been left money is about to deal with the tax office.
explanation.walkthrough: IR, the Inland Revenue, was the UK's tax collector until 2005.
explanation.definitionFit: An heir is the person who inherits property left in a will.

clue.text: Well-deserved good name — hurried to secure that

indicators.note: to secure says the first word holds the others safely inside it

parts.note: hared means ran fast, hurried
dear can mean kind or good, as in a good friend or a dear friend

explanation.surface: Someone rushed to protect their well-earned good reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: HARED holds DEAR and N: HAR-DEARN-ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard-earned praise or money is gained through great effort, so it is well-deserved.

clue.text: University in a second study, normally

indicators.note: in says the university letter goes inside the word for study

parts.note: a perusal is a careful reading or study

explanation.surface: A university student spends a second year studying as normal.
explanation.walkthrough: A and S come first; U goes into PERUSAL to make PERUSUAL.
explanation.definitionFit: As per usual is an informal phrase meaning in the customary way, as always.

clue.text: Himalayan creature still heading for India

parts.note: still in the sense of up to now means yet

indicators.note: heading for says take only the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A Himalayan creature is still making its way toward India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading for' looks like a direction of travel but means the first letter of India.
explanation.definitionFit: The yeti is the legendary ape-like abominable snowman said to live in the Himalayas.

clue.text: Drinker returned to work with plants

indicators.note: returned says the word for a drinker is read backwards

parts.note: a toper is a habitual heavy drinker

explanation.surface: A drinker goes back to his gardening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns TOPER round.
explanation.definitionFit: To repot is to move a plant into a new pot, a gardening task.

clue.text: Crossword's beginning with sad clues, badly written — they lead nowhere

indicators.note: beginning says take only the opening letter of the word
badly written says the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A crossword that opens with poorly written clues goes nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: C, from 'Crossword's beginning', comes first; 'badly written' rearranges SAD CLUES to give ULSDESAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Culs-de-sac are dead-end streets, closed at one end, so they lead to no through route.

clue.text: Pupil (not first) on sex trips — removal from school ensues

indicators.note: trips suggests the letters stumbling and falling into a new order
not first says the opening letter of the word is dropped

explanation.surface: A pupil goes on sex trips and is thrown out of school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not first' drops P from PUPIL to leave UPIL; 'trips' rearranges UPIL with ON and SEX.
explanation.definitionFit: Expulsion is the act of formally throwing a pupil out of a school.

clue.text: Relaxed line that is backed? Certainly

indicators.note: backed says the abbreviation for that is runs in reverse

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation for id est, Latin for that is
surely is an exclamation of agreement, certainly

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a line is truly supported and gets a relaxed yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns IE into EI: L-EI-SURELY.
explanation.definitionFit: Leisurely means unhurried and easygoing, in a relaxed manner.

clue.text: Girl allows getting stuck into beer when it's raised

indicators.note: raised in a down clue says the whole assembly is read upwards
getting stuck into says the verb is placed inside the drink

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
lets means allows

explanation.surface: A girl tucks into a beer when the glass is lifted.
explanation.walkthrough: LETS goes into ALE to make ALLETSE; 'when it's raised' reads that upwards, giving the name of the heroine of Great Expectations.
explanation.definitionFit: Estella is a girl's name, best known from Dickens's Great Expectations.

clue.text: I have to follow the others in becoming unsettled

indicators.note: to follow says the second piece comes after the first

parts.note: the rest means the others, the remaining ones
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: Someone becomes restless at having to trail behind everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in becoming' only joins the wordplay to the definition; read 'becoming unsettled' as the state the answer names.
explanation.definitionFit: Restive means restless and fidgety, unable to keep calm or settled.

clue.text: A little kiss by son

indicators.note: by says the two pieces stand next to each other

parts.note: a peck is a quick light kiss

explanation.surface: A son gives a small kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A little' reads as part of 'a little kiss' but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A speck is a tiny spot or particle, the smallest bit of something.

clue.text: Show sympathy for what organist faces

explanation.walkthrough: The verb and the noun are spelt alike; the noun is the organ's keyboard desk.
explanation.definitionFit: To comfort someone is to show them sympathy, and an organ's keyboards and stops are housed in the panel the player sits facing.

clue.text: Engrave back sections of pocket watch

indicators.note: back sections of says take the final pair of letters from each word

explanation.surface: Someone is told to engrave the back of a pocket watch.
explanation.walkthrough: The last two letters of POCKET and of WATCH give ET and CH.
explanation.definitionFit: To etch is to cut a design into metal or glass, as an engraver does.

clue.text: Scavenger longing to tuck into first couple of hartebeest

indicators.note: to tuck into says the word for longing goes inside the opening letters
first couple of says take the opening two letters of the word

parts.note: a yen is a strong longing or desire

explanation.surface: A scavenger is eager to start eating a hartebeest.
explanation.walkthrough: A hartebeest is an African antelope; 'first couple of' takes two letters, not one.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyenas are African carnivores known for feeding on carcasses left by other animals.

clue.text: Make neater mines, later exploding

indicators.note: exploding suggests the mines blow apart and their letters land in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone tidies up mines that will explode later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exploding' rearranges MINES LATER.
explanation.definitionFit: To streamline something is to simplify it and make it more efficient and tidy.

clue.text: Notice the total here!

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, a public notice
the sum is the total

explanation.surface: A notice says the total is here.
explanation.walkthrough: Adsum is Latin for 'I am present', the reply once given in a school roll call, so it means 'here!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Adsum is the Latin roll-call answer meaning I am present.

clue.text: A tendency to nodding and winking?

definitions.text: A tendency to nodding and winking?

parts.words: A tendency to nodding and winking?
parts.note: nodding off and catching forty winks both describe dozing, not signalling with head and eye

explanation.surface: A habit of nodding and winking suggests secret signals.
explanation.walkthrough: Nods and winks look like gestures, but 'nod off' and 'forty winks' are both about dozing.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleepiness is drowsiness, the state in which a person keeps dropping off.

clue.text: No-one repelled about King being in club

indicators.note: being in says the king's letter is placed inside the other piece
repelled says the letters are pushed back the other way

parts.note: no is spelt as written and one is the Roman numeral I
R is the abbreviation for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: No-one is pushed back while the King is in the club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repelled' turns NO I into ION, and R goes inside it; 'about' is a link. An IRON is a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf an iron is a club with a metal head, used for shorter shots.

clue.text: Public show is not held in delightful place

indicators.note: not held in says the little word is no longer contained within the other

parts.note: paradise is a place of perfect delight

explanation.surface: A public show is not to be staged in a beauty spot.
explanation.walkthrough: IS is removed from PARADISE.
explanation.definitionFit: A parade is a public procession, a march or display put on for spectators.

clue.text: Spotted pieces played

parts.note: the tiles in this game are marked with spots, and the clue describes them laid out in play

explanation.surface: Spotted tiles are laid down in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: The name of the spotted tiles is also the name of the game played with them.
explanation.definitionFit: Small oblong tiles marked with pips are laid end to end in a game of the same name.
